title: Consumer Contract Lock
description: The immutable dependency record a consuming repository keeps to declare which contracts release it was validated against. Language-neutral by design: it is a data file validated in the consumer's CI, never an import mechanism, and this repository never becomes a runtime library. Pinning a version alone is not enough - integrity hashes are what make the pin verifiable rather than merely stated.

dependencies.title: Pinned dependencies
dependencies.description: Contract dependencies by repository name. At M0 only ai-business-contracts is pinnable, and the property name is fixed so a lock cannot silently point at some other producer.

consumer.title: Consuming repository
consumer.description: Which repository this lock belongs to. Present so a gate reading many locks can attribute a mismatch.

pin.title: Release pin
pin.description: An exact, immutable reference to one published contracts release.

version.title: Pinned version
version.description: The exact released version. Not a range, not a prefix: a floating range would let the dependency change without the lock changing, which defeats the lock.

source.title: Dependency source
source.description: Where the artifact came from. Only 'release' is permitted for a production dependency. A mutable branch is not a source a checksum can describe, so the closed enum is what makes the prohibition enforceable rather than advisory.

manifest_sha256.title: Manifest checksum
manifest_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the release manifest the consumer validated against.

bundle_sha256.title: Bundle checksum
bundle_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the contract bundle archive the consumer validated against.

required_contracts.title: Required contract identifiers
required_contracts.description: Contract identifiers this consumer depends on. The platform gate checks each one exists in the pinned release, so a consumer discovers a removed contract at gate time rather than at runtime.
